text: He has married many couples but has never married himself. He wears a robe and presides over a courtroom. Who is he?
why_original_fails: A priest does not preside over a courtroom; a judge does and can officiate marriages.
original_text: He has married many women but has never married.

text: What do you throw out to use and take in when you're done, and it has a hook at the end?
why_original_fails: An anchor has no hook at the end; a fishing line does and is cast out and reeled in.
original_text: What do you throw out to use and take in when you're done?

text: You see me once in July, twice in August, and not at all in May. What am I?
why_original_fails: 'July' has one U, 'August' two, 'May' none; N appears in none of these months.
original_text: You see me once in June, twice in November, and not at all in May. What am I?

text: What four-letter word becomes longer when you add two letters to it?
why_original_fails: 'Short' has five letters and adding 'er' makes 'shorter', not 'longer'; 'long' plus 'er' is 'longer'.
original_text: What five-letter word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?

text: I have a neck but no head. I have a body but no arms. I have a bottom but no legs. I make music when my strings are plucked. What am I?
why_original_fails: A bottle has no strings; a guitar has a neck, a body, a bottom and strings.
original_text: I have a neck but no head. I have a body but no arm. I have a bottom but no leg.

text: What is pronounced like one letter, written with three letters, and is a hot drink?
why_original_fails: 'Eye' is not a drink; 'tea' is pronounced like the letter T, has three letters, and is a hot drink.
original_text: What is pronounced like one letter, written with three letters. And belongs to all animals?

text: What has to be broken before you can use it, and grows on a palm tree?
why_original_fails: Eggs do not grow on palm trees; coconuts do and must be broken open.
original_text: What has to be broken before you can use it?

text: What can you catch but not throw, and has fins and scales?
why_original_fails: A cold has no fins or scales; a fish does and is caught, not thrown.
original_text: What can you catch but not throw?

text: Mr. and Mrs. Mustard have six daughters, and each daughter has two brothers. How many people are in the Mustard family?
why_original_fails: Two shared brothers plus six daughters plus two parents is ten, not nine.
original_text: Mr. and Mrs. Mustard have six daughters, and each daughter has one brother. How many people are in the Mustard family?

text: Lucy's father has five daughters: Nana, Nene, Nini, Nono. What is the name of the fifth daughter?
why_original_fails: The father in the text is Lucy's, so the unnamed daughter is Lucy, not Mary.
original_text: Mary's father has five daughters: Nana, Nene, Nini, Nono. What is the name of the fifth daughter?

text: I have keys but no locks. I have space but no room. You can enter, but you can't go outside. I have 88 keys and I make music. What am I?
why_original_fails: A computer keyboard has more than 88 keys and makes no music; 88 keys that make music is a piano.
original_text: I have keys but no locks. I have space but no room. You can enter, but you can't go outside. What am I?

text: What has a neck but no head, and you wear it?
why_original_fails: A bottle is not worn; a shirt has a neck and is.
original_text: What has a neck but no head, and wears a cap?

text: What flies without wings and is held by a string?
why_original_fails: Time is not held by a string; a kite (or a balloon) flies without wings on one.
original_text: What flies without wings?

text: A bat and a ball cost $1.20 in total. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?
why_original_fails: With a $1.20 total, ball + (ball + 1.00) = 1.20 gives 10 cents, not 5.
original_text: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 in total. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?

text: I'm tall when I'm young, and I'm short when I'm old, and you sharpen me to write. What am I?
why_original_fails: A candle is not sharpened to write; the clause pins pencil, which also shortens with use.
original_text: I'm tall when I'm young, and I'm short when I'm old. What am I?

text: What goes up when the rain comes down, and flows between two banks?
why_original_fails: An umbrella does not flow between banks; a river rises when it rains.
original_text: What goes up when the rain comes down?

text: If it takes 5 machines 5 minutes to make 5 widgets, how long would it take 100 machines to make 200 widgets?
why_original_fails: Each machine makes one widget per 5 minutes; 100 machines make 100 widgets per 5 minutes, so 200 take 10 minutes.
original_text: If it takes 5 machines 5 minutes to make 5 widgets, how long would it take 100 machines to make 100 widgets?

text: Take off my skin, I won't cry, and neither will you. I am yellow and curved. What am I?
why_original_fails: Peeling an onion makes you cry; a yellow, curved fruit peeled without tears is a banana.
original_text: Take off my skin, I won't cry, but you will.

text: What is that over the head and under the hat, on a completely bald man?
why_original_fails: A bald man has no hair; what is under his hat is bare scalp, or nothing.
original_text: What is that over the head and under the hat?

text: I have two wings and I do fly. I never laugh and never cry. I carry people through the sky. What am I?
why_original_fails: A windmill has four wings and cannot fly; a two-winged flier that carries people is an airplane.
original_text: I have four wings but cannot fly. I never laugh and never cry. On the same spot always found, toiling away with little sound.

text: I sleep by day, I fly by night. I have feathers to aid my flight. What am I?
why_original_fails: A bat has no feathers; a nocturnal flier with feathers is an owl.
original_text: I sleep by day, I fly by night. I have no feathers to aid my flight.

text: I have feathers to help me fly. I have a body and head, but I'm not alive. It is your strength which determines how far I go. You hold me in your hand, and then you throw me. What am I?
why_original_fails: An arrow is never thrown, it is shot; a feathered thing thrown by hand is a dart.
original_text: I have many feathers to help me fly. I have a body and head, but I'm not alive. It is your strength which determines how far I go. You can hold me in your hand, but I'm never thrown.

text: They have flesh and bone, and skin of their own. They have fingers and thumbs, and are on the ends of your arms. What are they?
why_original_fails: Gloves have no flesh or bone; hands have both and end the arms.
original_text: They have not flesh, nor feathers, nor scales, nor bone. Yet they have fingers and thumbs of their own.

text: A mother and her son are in a car accident. The mother dies at the scene and the son is rushed to the hospital. At the hospital the surgeon looks at the boy and says, "I cannot operate on this boy, he is my son." How is this possible?
answer: the surgeon is the boy's father
why_original_fails: The mother is dead, so the surgeon cannot be the mother; a parent who is alive and calls him 'my son' is the father.
original_text: A father and his son are in a car accident. The father dies at the scene and the son is rushed to the hospital. At the hospital the surgeon looks at the boy and says, "I cannot operate on this boy, he is my son." How is this possible?
original_answer: the surgeon is the boy's mother

jalapeno:DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.final: The surgeon is the boy's father.
jalapeno:DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.label: correct

jalapeno:GLM-5.3-Flash.final: The surgeon is the boy's father.
jalapeno:GLM-5.3-Flash.label: correct

jalapeno:Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.final: The surgeon is the boy's father
jalapeno:Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.label: correct

text: What has bark and bites?
why_original_fails: A tree does not bite; a dog barks and bites.
original_text: What has bark but no bite?

text: If there are three apples and you take away two, how many apples are left?
why_original_fails: The question asks what is left, not what you have: three minus two is one.
original_text: If there are three apples and you take away two, how many apples do you have?

text: Divide 30 by half and subtract ten. What do you get?
why_original_fails: 30 divided by one half is 60; subtracting ten gives 50, not 70.
original_text: Divide 30 by half and add ten. What do you get?

text: In a lake, there is a patch of lily pads. Every day, the patch doubles in size. If it takes 48 days for the patch to cover the entire lake, how long would it take for the patch to cover a quarter of the lake?
why_original_fails: Two doublings before day 48 is a quarter, so day 46, not 47.
original_text: In a lake, there is a patch of lily pads. Every day, the patch doubles in size. If it takes 48 days for the patch to cover the entire lake, how long would it take for the patch to cover half of the lake?

text: What can you hold in your left hand but never in your right hand?
why_original_fails: The hands are swapped in the question, so the answer is the right hand, not the left.
original_text: What can you hold in your right hand but never in your left hand?

text: You throw away the outside and cook the inside. Then you eat the outside and throw away the inside. What did you throw away last?
why_original_fails: The question asks what was thrown away last, the cob; 'corn' is what was eaten.
original_text: You throw away the outside and cook the inside. Then you eat the outside and throw away the inside. What did you eat?

text: If you overtake the person in second place in a race, what place is the person you just overtook in now?
why_original_fails: The question is about the runner overtaken, who drops from second to third.
original_text: If you overtake the person in second place in a race, what place are you in?

text: An electric train is travelling north at 100 miles per hour. The wind is blowing from the east. In which direction is the train travelling?
why_original_fails: The question asks the train's direction, stated as north; the smoke answer is to a different question.
original_text: An electric train is travelling north at 100 miles per hour. The wind is blowing from the east. Which way does the smoke blow?

text: A farmer has 17 sheep and all but 9 die. How many sheep died?
why_original_fails: The question asks how many died: 17 minus the 9 survivors is 8.
original_text: A farmer has 17 sheep and all but 9 die. How many sheep are left?

text: Johnny's mother had three children. The first child was named April. The second child was named May. The third child was named June. What was the name of the third child?
why_original_fails: The third child's name is given in the text as June; Johnny would be a fourth child.
original_text: Johnny's mother had three children. The first child was named April. The second child was named May. What was the third child's name?

text: Mary's father has five daughters: Nana, Nene, Nini, Nono, and Nunu. What is the name of the fifth daughter?
why_original_fails: All five daughters are named in the text; the fifth is Nunu, and Mary would be a sixth.
original_text: Mary's father has five daughters: Nana, Nene, Nini, Nono. What is the name of the fifth daughter?

text: If a red house is made of red bricks and a blue house is made of blue bricks, what is a red house made of?
why_original_fails: The text says a red house is made of red bricks; 'glass' answers the greenhouse pun that is no longer asked.
original_text: If a red house is made of red bricks and a blue house is made of blue bricks, what is a greenhouse made of?

text: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 in total. The bat costs $1.00. How much does the ball cost?
why_original_fails: The bat's price is given outright as $1.00, so the ball is $1.10 minus $1.00, which is 10 cents.
original_text: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 in total. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?

text: If a red house is made of red bricks and a blue house is made of blue bricks, what is a yellow house made of?
why_original_fails: 'Yellow house' has no pun; by the stated pattern it is made of yellow bricks, not glass.
original_text: If a red house is made of red bricks and a blue house is made of blue bricks, what is a greenhouse made of?

text: How many animals of each kind did Noah take on the ark?
why_original_fails: The name is Noah, so the trick is gone and the story's answer, two of each, applies.
original_text: How many animals of each kind did Moses take on the ark?

jalapeno:GLM-5.3-Flash.final: Seven of clean animals, two of unclean
jalapeno:GLM-5.3-Flash.label: correct

text: Two fathers and two sons go fishing. Each of them catches one fish, and they bring home four fish. How many people went fishing?
why_original_fails: Four fish, one each, means four people; the three-person trick no longer fits.
original_text: Two fathers and two sons go fishing. Each of them catches one fish, but they bring home only three fish. How is this possible?
original_answer: they are a grandfather, a father and a son
original_aliases: there are only three of them
